draft.title: Transport systems in plants
card: Plants have tubes that carry materials around the plant, much as blood vessels do in animals. The tubes are grouped in bundles that run through the roots, stems and leaves.
tubes that carry water and minerals from the roots up to the stem and leaves.
tubes that carry sugars made in the leaves to the rest of the plant, such as the roots and growing tips.
Leaves make sugars by photosynthesis. Roots take in water and minerals from the soil. Each tube type moves its materials from where they are made or taken in to where they are needed.
draft.remember: Xylem moves water and minerals up from the roots. Phloem moves sugars from the leaves.

a.q: Which tissue carries the water that a tree's roots take in from the soil up to its leaves?
opts: Xylem
Phloem
Alveoli
Arteries
a.why: Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots up to the stem and leaves. Phloem is tempting because it is also a plant transport tissue, but it carries sugars made in the leaves.
a.clue: Think about the direction the water travels and which tubes go that way.

b.q: Sam cuts a ring of bark and phloem from around a young tree's trunk. Xylem is left untouched. Sugars from the leaves can no longer reach the roots. What is the best explanation?
opts: Phloem carries sugars from the leaves and has been cut
Xylem carries sugars from the leaves and has been cut
Phloem carries water from the roots and has been cut
Xylem carries minerals to the roots and has been cut
b.why: Phloem carries the sugars made in the leaves to the rest of the plant, so cutting it stops sugars reaching the roots. Xylem was left untouched, and it carries water and minerals up, not sugars down.
b.clue: Which tissue was cut, and what does that tissue carry?

b.best: Phloem carries sugars from the leaves and has been cut

problems.detail: The stem says only bark and phloem were cut and xylem was left untouched. That rules out both 'Xylem ... has been cut' options without any knowledge of what xylem does. The right option also repeats the stem's phrase 'sugars from the leaves', so a student can pick it by word-matching. Only the choice between the two phloem options tests the idea.

Both questions and the whys call xylem and phloem a 'tissue', but the card only calls them 'tubes'. Some Year 8 students may not link the two words. Calling them tissues on the card, or saying 'tubes' in the question, would fix this.

a.q: A tree's leaves need a steady supply of water. Which tissue brings this water to them?
opts: Xylem
Phloem
Alveoli
Capillaries
a.why: Water is taken in by the roots, and xylem carries it up to the stem and leaves. Phloem is tempting because it is also a plant transport tissue, but it carries sugars made in the leaves.
a.clue: Where does a tree get its water from?

b.q: A potato plant stores food in potatoes that grow under the ground. The food is made from sugars. Which tissue brings the sugars, and from where?
opts: Phloem, bringing them from the leaves
Xylem, bringing them from the leaves
Phloem, bringing them from the soil
Xylem, bringing them from the soil
b.why: Sugars are made in the leaves by photosynthesis, and phloem carries them to other parts of the plant. Xylem from the soil is tempting because potatoes are underground, but roots take in water and minerals from the soil, not sugars.
b.clue: Which part of the plant makes sugars?

b.best: Phloem, bringing them from the leaves
